text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
WellAttended(wedding) ::: wedding is well-attended.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
HasWedding(wedding) ::: x has a wedding.
John ::: the individual John.

Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others make wedding plans.
∀x (∃w (Wedding(w) ∧ WellAttended(w) ∧ Attends(x, w))) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to their ceremony.
∃x (Wedding(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) → ∃w (Wedding(w) ∧ WellAttended(w)) ::: People with larger families have well-attended weddings.
If(Engaged(john)) → (¬Invite(john, friends) ∧ WeddingPlans(john)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and makes wedding plans.
LargerFamily(john) → (∃w (Wedding(w) ∧ WellAttended(w))) ∨ (∃y (Invite(john, y))) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.

Conclusion:
Engaged(john) ::: John is engaged.
